rfc8520.title: Manufacturer Usage Description Specification

group.name: Operations and Management Area Working Group

rfc8520.abstract:
This memo specifies a component-based architecture for Manufacturer Usage Descriptions (MUDs). The goal of MUD is to provide a means for end devices to signal to the network what sort of access and network functionality they require to properly function. The initial focus is on access control. Later work can delve into other aspects.

 This memo specifies two YANG modules, IPv4 and IPv6 DHCP options, a Link Layer Discovery Protocol (LLDP) TLV, a URL, an X.509 certificate extension, and a means to sign and verify the descriptions.

rfc9238.title: Loading Manufacturer Usage Description (MUD) URLs from QR Codes
rfc9238.abstract:
This informational document details a protocol to load Manufacturer Usage Description (MUD) definitions from RFC 8520 for devices that do not have them integrated.

 This document is published to inform the Internet community of this mechanism to allow interoperability and to serve as a basis of other standards work if there is interest.

rfc9726.title: Operational Considerations for Use of DNS in Internet of Things (IoT) Devices

group.name: Operations and Management Area Working Group

rfc9726.abstract:
This document details considerations about how Internet of Things (IoT) devices use IP addresses and DNS names. These concerns become acute as network operators begin deploying Manufacturer Usage Descriptions (MUD), as specified in RFC 8520, to control device access.

 Also, this document makes recommendations on when and how to use DNS names in MUD files.

rfc9761.title: Manufacturer Usage Description (MUD) for TLS and DTLS Profiles for Internet of Things (IoT) Devices

group.name: Operations and Management Area Working Group

rfc9761.abstract: This memo extends the Manufacturer Usage Description (MUD) specification to allow manufacturers to define TLS and DTLS profile parameters.  This allows a network security service to identify unexpected (D)TLS usage, which can indicate the presence of unauthorized software, malware, or security policy-violating traffic on an endpoint.
